p.i: Sic Pharao commissa petens sacra agmina Mosi, Factus Erythræi piscibus esca maris.
Hostis vterque Dei sanctorum & gentis vterque, Curribus hic multis, nauibus ille potens.
Exitio currus nauésque feruntur eodem, Sanguinis vt satiet purior vnda sitim, Et regredi vt posset (quoniam est aggressor vterque) Neutri commoti Numinis ira dedit.
Sic reliquas auidus Mundi sibi subdere gentes Subiicit Anglorum colla superba iugo.
Quíque alios spreuit, vulgi fit fabula, vt alta Qui viuens petiit, mortuus ima petat.
Quinetiam ardenti mediis occurrit in vndis Non minus ardescens & ferus ille Draco: Iste quidem patriæ succensus amore tuendæ, Ille Anglas sitiens totus auarus opes.
Sic flammæ vltrices slammas superastis auaras: Et Deus est flammis, est quoque vi[?]tor aquis.
PRINCEPS Maurici, heroum qui sanguiné natus Augustum virtute genus virtute coronas: Cuius crefcentis splendor magis aureus auro Crefcit, vt inuideant aurati lumina secli.

page.notes: The verse is set as continuous lines; stanza division follows sense. The "i" in "vitior" and "quo" in the verse may be misprinted; "vi[?]tor" is read as printed with a doubtful letter. The initial P of "PRINCEPS" is a large initial. The "è"/"é" accents in "sanguiné" and "nauésque" are read from the scan and may be inexact. The running head "IBERICA." is copied as printed. The catchword "Fœ-" carries its hyphen as printed.
